solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seaman entering boozer to see what's afoot?

indicators.note: the seaman goes into the boozer, so his letters sit inside the drinker's

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard, a boozer
AB, able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor walks into a pub, perhaps to find out what's going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' looks like a pub, but here it is the drinker, SOT. 'What's afoot?' is a punning definition: something worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, literally something found on a foot.

clue.text: House group D?

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
a circle is a group of people

explanation.surface: A puzzling label: a housing estate's group D?
explanation.walkthrough: The letter D is shaped like half a circle; the question mark flags the visual definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital D is drawn as a straight line closed by a half-round curve.

clue.text: Exile's collar turned up

indicators.note: in a down answer, read from bottom to top

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to nab them

explanation.surface: An exile's shirt collar was turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban someone can mean to banish or exile them.

clue.text: Spanish fighter quickly ran mounted troops

parts.note: tore means rushed or ran fast

indicators.note: in a down answer, mounted reads upwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A Spanish soldier dashing away from cavalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted troops' suggests cavalry; 'mounted' is the turn-round signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A torero is a bullfighter in Spain, especially one on foot.

clue.text: Craftsman penning unlimited poems in rocker

indicators.note: the trimmed poems are placed in the rocker, inside its letters

parts.note: something that rocks or shakes is a shaker

indicators.note: without its limits, the word poems loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An artisan writing poems while sitting in a rocking chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' only links the craftsman to the wordplay; 'rocker' looks like a chair or a musician but is one who shakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler who makes footwear is a traditional craftsman.

clue.text: Canvasses on display, reputable Society taking the lead

indicators.note: these letters go ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a sound firm is reliable or reputable
out means visible or on show

explanation.surface: A respectable society leads the way in canvassing for votes.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass opinion is to sound people out, asking what they think.

clue.text: Matter bringing down temperature of the eye

indicators.note: in a down answer, the letter is moved lower in the word

parts.note: a topic is a subject or matter

explanation.surface: Something that lowers the temperature of the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing down' moves T from first to third place, TOPIC to OPTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective meaning relating to the eye or to vision.

clue.text: Campaigns fail, stopped by endless din from below

indicators.note: the word for fail is plugged by the other piece

parts.note: to miss is to fail to hit

indicators.note: in a down answer, reading upwards
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: noise is din

explanation.surface: Military campaigns fail, halted by constant noise from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts NOISE to NOIS, which 'from below' turns into SION, placed in MIS-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Missions are operations or campaigns, as in bombing missions.

clue.text: Unorthodox vessel's link to betel nuts

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A strange container connected to betel nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betel nuts' reads as a product, but 'nuts' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Klein bottle is a mathematical surface with no inside or outside, a very strange container.

clue.text: Regular payment slashed

definitions.meaning: the money a tenant pays monthly to a landlord
torn or ripped open, past tense of rend

explanation.surface: A regular payment that has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is both a tenant's periodic payment and the past participle of rend, meaning torn.

clue.text: Small case for diamonds?

definitions.note: diamonds is one example, hence the question mark

parts.note: minor means small or lesser
a lawsuit is a legal case

explanation.surface: A little box to keep jewels in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case for diamonds' suggests a jewel box; in bridge, diamonds and clubs are the lower-ranking suits.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, diamonds is one of the two lower-scoring suits, an example of the category.

clue.text: Lustre perceived when heroin's injected

indicators.note: the drug is put into the other word, as with a needle

parts.note: seen means perceived
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A druggy glow noticed when someone shoots up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre and sheen are synonyms for a soft shine on a surface.

clue.text: Police officer probing one element of Labour opposition

indicators.note: the officer pokes into the other piece, ending up inside it

parts.note: in childbirth, labour is made up of contractions
DI, Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective investigating a faction of the Labour Party that opposes something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks political, but it is childbirth; a contraction is one part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A contradiction is a denial or opposing statement, so it amounts to opposition.

clue.text: Don't stop English composer hiding for instance in Tyneside

indicators.note: the rest goes inside the region's letters

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

indicators.note: the composer conceals the phrase within him

parts.note: Verdi, the Italian opera composer
say means for example

explanation.surface: An English composer hiding in Newcastle, refusing to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English composer' looks like one person (Elgar?), but English is just E and the composer is the Italian Verdi.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges someone to keep going and never give up, the same as an order to persevere.

clue.text: Comprehensive strike has support of illegitimate offspring

indicators.note: in a down answer, the second piece sits under the first, holding it up

parts.note: a blow is a strike
a by-blow is an old word for a child born out of wedlock

explanation.surface: A total strike backed by an illegitimate child.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed, step-by-step account is a thorough and comprehensive one.

clue.text: Party threatening to ditch leader

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its leader

parts.note: a grave situation is serious or threatening

explanation.surface: A party that is menacing to throw out its leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large dance party, typically with electronic music.

clue.text: Natural fibre, too much found in racket left on court

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another follows it
the excess sits inside the racket

parts.note: a con is a swindle or racket
OTT, over the top
to woo is to court romantically

explanation.surface: Too much fibre appears in a tennis racket left on the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' and 'court' paint tennis, but racket is a swindle (CON) and court is to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton wool is raw cotton fluff, a natural plant fibre.

clue.text: Her vital statistics initially disrupted play

indicators.note: thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged
just the opening letter of statistics

explanation.surface: A woman's measurements upset a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital statistics' is a dated phrase for a woman's measurements. HER VITAL is the anagram, signalled by 'disrupted'; S stands beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's 1775 comedy is a well-known stage play.

clue.text: Dazzling feature of church in India

indicators.note: the church's feature is put inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a spire is a feature of many churches

explanation.surface: A dazzling church tower in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant, inspired performance is dazzling in its quality.

clue.text: Visual aids having setter long for correction?

indicators.note: the letters need correcting into another order

explanation.surface: A crossword setter wanting glasses to fix their eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SETTER LONG, signalled by 'correction', also hints at vision correction.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorgnettes are spectacles held up on a handle, an aid to seeing.

clue.text: Pack animals to watch bears

indicators.note: the phrase carries the answer within it, as one bears a load

explanation.surface: Pack animals to keep an eye on bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like animals, but it means carries.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow luggage is to pack it away.

clue.text: Departs, with inclination to wave

parts.note: D, the abbreviation for departs in timetables
an angle is a slope or inclination

explanation.surface: Someone leaves, inclined to wave goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle something is to swing or wave it loosely in the air.

clue.text: Dad recalled agent introducing one couple, fifty or so

indicators.note: called back, so the word for father is turned around

parts.note: pa is father

indicators.note: the agent brings the other letters into its middle

parts.note: a proxy acts on another's behalf
I is the Roman numeral one
to mate is to couple
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Father remembered an agent who introduced about fifty couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifty or so' looks like one phrase; fifty is L and 'or so' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding 'or so' to a number means roughly, the same as saying about.

clue.text: Auditor's dealing with file at the appropriate time

indicators.note: a hearer's version, what the listener takes in

parts.note: on means dealing with, and a file is a queue, a line of people

explanation.surface: An accountant handling a file at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant, but it means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who enters exactly on the signal is perfectly timed.

clue.text: Island shot guards Down Under

indicators.note: the word for a shot encloses the other piece

parts.note: a go is a try or shot
Oz is informal for Australia

explanation.surface: An island where shots protect Australians.
explanation.definitionFit: Gozo is the second-largest island of the Maltese archipelago.

clue.text: Senior retired Liberal in fashion again

indicators.note: the party letter goes inside the turned-round word
drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to redo is to make or fashion again

explanation.surface: An elderly retired Liberal politician back in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' fits the senior Liberal, but it is the turn-round signal: REDO read backwards gives ODER.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior means greater in age, which is what the comparative of old says.

clue.text: Almost complete backing for exhibit in church showing conversions?

indicators.note: the shortened word comes at the back, after the rest
the exhibit goes inside the church

parts.note: CE, Church of England
to hang a picture is to exhibit it

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: Supporting an exhibition in a church about religious conversions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conversions' suggests religion in a church, but it simply means changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something changeful keeps altering, constantly undergoing conversions from one form to another.

clue.text: Rage following promotion

parts.note: an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: Anger after a career promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rage' looks like anger, but here it means a craze.
explanation.definitionFit: A rage is a craze, something all the rage briefly fashionable.

clue.text: During many deliveries, Dr West stripped off outer garb

indicators.note: the doctor sits within the deliveries, inside the word

parts.note: in cricket an over is six deliveries, so overs are many
taken as written, the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: the word West loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A doctor named West undresses while a long spell of bowling goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled ('deliveries').
explanation.definitionFit: An overdress is a dress worn over other clothes, an outer garment.

clue.text: Limit old women's fund

parts.note: an end is a boundary or limit
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A cap on a pension fund for older women.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to provide money for, as in funding a hospital wing or college chair.
